_note: version, anchor and why are notes for humans - nothing executes them. paths/run/always/default/unmapped drive the Stop gate; agents drives /crew:review; environments drives /crew:promote. agents may name ANY installed subagent, not only crew's own - a bare name resolves to crew's role first, then to any other installed agent. One this machine lacks is reported as a gap, never skipped silently.

rules.why: fmt/validate catch syntax; tflint catches deprecated syntax and undocumented variables; terraform-docs --output-check FAILS when the README is stale instead of rewriting it - a gate that writes to the tree makes README.md a changed file on the next run, which trips unmapped:fail in a loop
Lambda handlers are orchestration; smoke proves the CSV-to-stg round trip still works
business logic lives in procedures; fresh apply catches ordering, rollback proves the down path, smoke proves data still moves
style changes are invisible to API checks; visual baselines are the only thing that sees them

permission changes need a scanner and a second pair of eyes, not just fmt. Two agents on purpose and they are not redundant: crew's security reads THIS diff for what it newly makes reachable, the domain auditor reads the resulting permission model for whether it is defensible at all. Drop the second name if it is not installed here - a rule that asks every time and never gets it is noise in metrics.md

these run with real privilege on domain-joined hosts, where a linter sees style and not blast radius. Example of naming a specialist crew does not ship - resolution falls through to any installed agent of that name
documentation. Listed so it does not trip unmapped:fail - deliberately unchecked, not forgotten

development.rollbackReason: dev is rebuilt on every push; there is nothing to roll back to

qa.rollbackReason: qa is rebuilt from the latest development deploy; there is nothing to roll back to
